topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening introduces the lecture's scope, links it to histopathology practicals, and outlines the day's learning objectives.

topics.label: Discovery of cellular oncogenes and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the study of tumor viruses revealed endogenous cellular genes that drive cancer and provided experimental assays to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Functional classifications and genetic mechanisms of cancer genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define how cancer-associated mutations alter gene function and cell cycle control, using pathways such as Rb and p53 to demonstrate dominance, recessiveness, and allele dosage.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genomic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific defects in DNA repair pathways, replication, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the sequential accumulation or inheritance of mutations accelerates tumor development and influences malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The closing concludes the lecture, recommends background reading, and previews the next lecture's topic.
